name: Seraiah (Brother of Baruch)
title: Quartermaster and Messenger
summary: Seraiah was the son of Neriah and brother to the prophet Jeremiah's scribe, Baruch. He served as quartermaster under King Zedekiah and was commissioned by Jeremiah to bring a prophetic scroll to Babylon containing words of judgment against the city. His role illustrates how God's word was to be preserved and proclaimed even during exile.

keyEvents.title: Journey to Babylon with King Zedekiah
keyEvents.description: Seraiah traveled to Babylon with King Zedekiah in his fourth year of reign, likely in connection with diplomatic negotiations or to demonstrate loyalty to Nebuchadnezzar.

keyEvents.title: Received the Scroll from Jeremiah
keyEvents.description: The prophet Jeremiah gave Seraiah a scroll containing all the disasters that would befall Babylon, along with instructions on what he was to do with it.

keyEvents.title: Mission to Read and Cast the Scroll
keyEvents.description: Seraiah was instructed to read the words aloud when he arrived in Babylon, then tie a stone to the scroll and cast it into the Euphrates as a prophetic sign of Babylon's coming downfall.
